newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev closes weaker at 361-365 per dollar.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev closes weaker at 361-365 per dollar.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev fell to 361-365 per dollar at the close of the interbank market from 357-361 morning levels due to a rise in foreign currency demand from final clients, dealers said.
"Large final clients were bidding for dollars amid a relatively low supply and lev lost around six (levs) from yesterday," a commercial bank dealer said.
The lev closed at 355-358 per dollar on Thursday. It traded at 345-355 on Monday.
The BNB was buying dollars around 355 in the morning, dealers said. Central bank officials declined comment.
The rise in foreign currency supply from final clients at the beginning of the week slowed down in the past two days and pressure on the lev resumed, dealers said.

Banks' final clients launched dollar sales at the beginning of the week in anticipation of a lev rise and because they needed levs for salaries and tax payments before the end of the month, traders said.

The lev suffered its worst setback last week, slumping from 275 to 395 per dollar before the BNB said last Friday it had agreed to coordinated action with commercial banks to prevent a new sharp fall in the lev.
Financial brokerages were denied buying foreign currency from banks as a result.
The central bank was buying dollars near 350 levs this week to replenish its foreign exchange reserves, absorbing part of the rise in dollar supply, traders said.
BNB forex reserves stood at $541 million at the end of October, down from $1.4 billion a year ago.
